label: One path per chat, no folders
text:
picked “One path per chat, no folders”
Board question: Pod chats in the bucket, new tree: your "Per-database epoch" pick collides with your Nov 2 order on incarnations. Which shape?
Card said: Pod chats in the bucket, new tree: a reviewer found that your "Per-database epoch" pick conflicts with your Nov 2 order to remove the incarnation machinery and keep it out of browsers and Macs. That reading of the Nov 2 order is the reviewer's, not your words. - **The conflict:** with per-database epochs, a chat's bucket path gets a new folder each time another pod takes the chat. Every reader, meaning the browser, share links and the journal replica, must then find the newest folder and switch to it live. Each cold open also costs a bucket listing. - **What is built today:** two open changes, one for writers and one for readers, implement the folders as picked. That is option 3. - **What each option moves:** the bucket layout for pod chats and the readers of it. Macs keep their one path in every option. - **The two open changes:** option 1 closes the reader change and keeps only the code deletions from the writer change. Option 2 reworks both to the cheaper folder layout. Option 3 lands both as they are. [Diagram: Pod chat bucket layout: the three shapes side by side](https://yasyf-forge-studio.tail71af5d.ts.net:61211/diagram/rmw5jo8es)
Card card-rmw5jo8es, block rmw5jo8es-choice, board d50e80e8-7ba3-491e-a0b2-8739e65f6ba9, Nov 6 2:28 PM PT.
The option he tapped, “One path per chat, no folders”, said: a restarted pod uploads nothing for a chat until it is taken, and the take already catches the bucket up. No epoch logic anywhere and readers stay as today. Cost: a chat on disk after a pod restart waits for its next take to upload
The card carried option 1 of pod-epoch-reuse-2's ask, cci #7970@3dd5e016: (Recommended) Keep one bucket path per chat with no folders. A restarted pod uploads nothing for a chat until that chat is taken. The take already compares the pod's copy with the bucket and catches it up ("just catch up", Oct 26/29). So boot does no per-chat bucket check, the browser and Macs keep today's reader unchanged, and no epoch or incarnation logic exists anywhere. Cost: a chat still on disk after a pod restart waits for its next take before it uploads. The code deletions in #52076 (found guard, holdFound) stay. #52130 closes.
